trustReason.publicTls: Agents trust this address without the LabTether CA.
trustReason.customTls: Agents check this certificate against the device’s own certificate store.
trustReason.labtetherCa: The install command adds the LabTether CA so the agent trusts the hub.
trustReason.plainHttp: Not encrypted. Use it only on a protected network, such as Tailscale.

linux.title: Linux install script
linux.pinnedCa: This address uses the LabTether CA. The command downloads and checks that CA before it runs the installer.
linux.customTls: This address uses your own TLS certificate. The device must already trust its certificate chain.
linux.vnc: Install VNC prerequisites for Remote View
linux.noToken: Without a token, the device waits for approval in LabTether.

proxmox.credentialsText: Use an API token such as labtether@pve!monitoring with read-only access to inventory and metrics.
proxmox.consoleLimit: Proxmox API tokens cannot open the Proxmox console (Proxmox bug 6079). Terminal sessions use SSH instead.
proxmox.skipApiTls: Skip TLS verification for the Proxmox API
proxmox.spiceBlocked: SPICE stays blocked: certificate details from an unverified API cannot be trusted.
proxmox.skipSpiceTls: Skip SPICE certificate verification. This is separate from the API setting and also needs LABTETHER_ALLOW_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=true on the hub.

pbs.credentialsText: Use an API token such as root@pam!labtether with read access to datastores and backups.
pbs.caPemHint: Paste the CA certificate chain to keep TLS verification on.

truenas.credentialsText: Create a TrueNAS API key for LabTether with read access to pools, datasets, SMART and system health.

docker.credentialsText: None needed. Containers come from LabTether agents that can reach Docker. Install at least one first.

portainer.credentialsText: Use a Portainer API key that can list environments. The token ID is optional and only labels the key in LabTether.

homeassistant.integrationText: Add the LabTether custom integration in Home Assistant, then enter the hub URL and owner token.
homeassistant.addonText: Runs the LabTether hub inside Home Assistant.
homeassistant.hubAddressHelp: Use the hub’s own address, not this console’s address. External and Tailscale addresses are listed. Type a LAN address if Home Assistant reaches the hub on your LAN.
homeassistant.reachNote: Home Assistant must reach this address. Use localhost only when both run on the same host.
homeassistant.credentialsText: In Home Assistant, create a long-lived access token for LabTether, for example named labtether_connector.
homeassistant.hubEmpty: Enter a hub address that Home Assistant can reach.
homeassistant.hubControl: The hub address contains control characters.
homeassistant.hubScheme: The hub address must start with http:// or https://.
homeassistant.hubCredentials: The hub address must not contain a username or password.
homeassistant.hubPath: The hub address must not contain a path, query or fragment.
homeassistant.hubPort: The hub address needs a valid port.
homeassistant.hubPlainHttp: Plain HTTP needs “Allow insecure HTTP” turned on in the Home Assistant integration.

manual.hostRequired: Enter the IP address or hostname.
manual.name: Device name
